Amazonian Iara of a black-water tributary, river-green and mirror-eyed, braiding water-lily stems through her hair, her reflection appearing first before her body surfaces in the warm shallow.
Ningyo of the Sea of Japan shallows, pearl-pale and omen-laden, rising at the approach of a storm fleet, face expressionless and ancient, eyes fixed on the admiral's lantern.
Mami Wata regal water-spirit of the Niger Delta, serpent-crowned and fragment-mirror-bright, combing long black hair in a tide-pool while a dredge-boat churns the far-water horizon.
Cornish mer-witch of a granite tide-pool grotto, herb-bedecked and salt-cracked, stirring a kelp-and-crabshell storm-charm with a driftwood rod in the grey pre-squall Atlantic light.
Polynesian mermaid-spirit of a Marquesas deep-channel, tā-moko-marked and whale-song-fluent, surfacing at the prow of a voyaging canoe to press her coral-crowned forehead to the hull.

Mediterranean siren of a Sicilian sea-cliff, golden-tongued and Renaissance-beautiful, ancient beyond counting, watching a lighthouse beam sweep across her cave-mouth with calm and unhurried violet eyes.
Young Andersen-lineage mermaid princess of a cold northern sea-king's court, longing-bright and restless, surfacing at dusk to trace the silhouette of a lit harbor.
Filipino Sirena of a Visayan reef shelf, ancient and luminescent, living-seaweed hair drifting with the tide, awakened by a solitary fisherman's lamp at full moon.
Mami Wata regal water-spirit of the Gulf of Guinea, serpent-coiled and imperious, mirror-and-comb gleaming, waiting for the devotee who brings the correct shrine offering.
Faroese selkie woman freshly shed of her sealskin on a basalt shore, melancholic and breathless, the folded pelt still warm beside her on the tide-wet rock.
Ancient Ningyo of the Kuroshio deep, pearl-pale and ageless, drifting through kelp-shadow, her presence alone enough to bend a fishing village's fate toward ruin or grace.
Slavic Rusalka of a Carpathian river bend, drowned-pale and cold-voiced, river-grass braided through her hair, drawing a wandering miller toward the water with a half-heard lullaby.
Greek Nereid of the Aegean at first light, bronze-skinned and dolphin-attended, daughter of an old sea-god's court, sea-foam threading her wake as she escorts a merchant galley.
Amazonian Iara of a blackwater river inlet, river-green hair and mirror-bright gaze, luring a rubber-tapper's canoe deeper into the flooded igapó with a song of sweet ruin.
Inuit polar mer-queen of the Beaufort Sea floor, scarred and immense, keeper of all sea-mammals, pack-ice shards tangled in her hair, watching a seal-hunter's kayak overhead.
Chinese Hai-Ren tear-pearling water-maiden of the South China Sea, silk-veiled and dragon-court-bound, weeping luminous pearls onto a shell-throne while a tribute envoy descends to bargain.
Polynesian mermaid-spirit of an atoll lagoon, tā-moko tattoos spiraling across her shoulders and jaw, coral-crowned and ceremonially grave, rising to bless an outrigger fleet at dawn.
Mediterranean siren of a sea-stack grotto, golden-throated and centuries-weary, long past luring sailors, now singing old hymns for passing petrels and the indifferent Ionian sun.
Andersen-lineage sea-king's youngest daughter of a deep Atlantic palace, wide-eyed and silver-finned, collecting shipwreck glass on a coral shelf before daring her first surface.
West African diaspora Mami Wata of a Caribbean harbor mouth, regal and serpent-draped, her mirror reflecting futures, granting prosperity to the market-woman who tends her riverside altar.
Scottish selkie elder of a Hebridean sea-cave, sealskin folded across her lap, centuries of grief layered in her gaze, watching a lighthouse tender approach the rocks at dusk.
Japanese Ningyo of an Edo-period fishing harbor, pearl-pale and omen-heavy, surfacing once at the harbor mouth, her appearance sending the village elder to the temple in cold dread.
Slavic Rusalka of a Volga shallows at midsummer, pale and languid, water-iris stems wound through her hair, singing a feast-night circle-dance melody to a stranded ferryboat crew.
Filipino Sirena of a Sulu Sea coral garden, luminous and slow-moving, cowrie-adorned and patient, surfacing to examine a diving boy who has found a pearl of unusual size.
Greek Naiad of an Arcadian spring-source, moss-green and softly radiant, freshwater-born and shy of salt, granting a shepherd's flock safe crossing through the flooded meadow ford.
Amazonian Iara of a várzea floodplain channel, honey-voiced and serene, green-haired and mirror-eyed, drawing a Jesuit cartographer's raft off-course with a melody of impossible sweetness.
Polynesian mermaid-spirit of a deep volcanic seamount, tā-moko-marked and authoritative, coral-crowned, surfacing to turn back a fishing canoe straying above a sacred breeding ground.
Mami Wata shrine-spirit of a Nigerian river delta, comb-and-mirror sovereign, serpent draped across both shoulders, accepting the woven cloth offering of a petitioner seeking a child.
Inuit polar mer-queen of a polynya beneath spring ice, vast and deliberate, seal-tending and powerful, extending a scarred hand to release the fish-schools toward a starving coastal camp.
Chinese Hai-Ren of a Tang-dynasty coral palace, silk-veiled and ceremonially precise, carrying pearl-tribute in a lacquered shell-box toward the dragon-king's audience chamber in the eastern deep.
Mediterranean siren of a Sicilian headland sea-cliff, golden-tongued and baroque in her sorrow, singing now only to the gulls, having outlived every sailor she once called to ruin.
